questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses offered, language taught in, and the possibly unique fact that had dear friends already in the Stuttgart-area

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Just the orientation accompanying the picking up of the student card etc., as well as the orientation for the philosophy department by your erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Perhaps too much repetition. I have been sent sooo many emails. And the same information was given upon arrival.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, if you have enough money. It was very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have a wife and child. Though "family-housing" was made available, it was too far away from the inner city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Their website for this, Alma, is very poorly designed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Find the website, find the right list in a maze of menus, scroll through every single course offered in the whole university, read up on the "codes" that signify what type of course it is, learn what that type of course entails, then simply click "apply".

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office / the erasmus office were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: completely

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply to a LOT of courses. Go to the first class of each one - they do not expect you to read anything by then. Just see what the course is ACTUALLY about (their descriptions on ALMA are sometimes wrong). Then talk to the professors too. The conditions that apply in principle to each type of course are not  followed by each teacher. And the CP amount is not set - you can make special arrangements with each professor.

questions.answer: Only the former two. But I am not sure they will be back - at least not the second one.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
What I said under "What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *"

Visit other cities.

Take many small courses, not few big ones. Their otherwise strict participation condition is not upheld.
